# DropSpace v0.3.0-preview.12 — Receiver memory hardening

<!-- update-summary: Preview.12 adds bounded streamed encrypted-share receiver downloads and extends Preview.11 audit hardening without changing the Windows compatibility contract. -->

Preview.12 extends the Preview.11 full-audit hardening boundary for encrypted Internet Share downloads.

## Encrypted Share receiver

- Browsers with the File System Access API now decrypt and write one chunk at a time directly to a user-selected destination.
- Receiver integrity validation uses an incremental SHA-256 implementation, so a large download is not duplicated into a full in-memory Blob just to calculate its digest.
- Browsers without file streaming support use an explicit 256 MiB in-memory fallback limit instead of attempting an unbounded allocation. Fallback downloads are serialized across the page through temporary Blob URL cleanup, and their buttons are disabled while active.
- A failed integrity check aborts the selected destination and does not expose a corrupted file.
- The receiver keeps the per-response nonce CSP and never turns displayName into HTML.

## Validation boundary

- Worker module parsing and Worker coordinator regression tests run in CI.
- Receiver generation is covered for nonce CSP, removal of unsafe-inline, the streaming file-picker path, and the bounded fallback contract.
- The reference Worker still requires the SHARE_COORDINATOR Durable Object binding and deployment-level abuse/rate-limit controls.
- This Preview remains CONDITIONAL until real Windows OS/DPI/native Smart Drag evidence and operator-deployed Worker/browser acceptance are recorded.

Stable-channel users will not receive this Preview. Select the Preview channel only to test the hardening behavior.
